learning_objectives: Understand and use turkish vowels and casing.
scope_included: recognize the eight vowels, front and back groups, and the distinct I, İ, ı and i letters

references.title: Türkiye Maarif Vakfı: Türkçenin Yabancı Dil Olarak Öğretimi Programı

skills.description_en: Recognise the eight written Turkish vowels in familiar A1 words.
Identify back vowels a, ı, o, u and front vowels e, i, ö, ü.
Distinguish dotted and dotless I/i and match uppercase and lowercase vowels.
Supply the exact written vowel in an A1 word.

lesson.short_explanation_en: Turkish has eight vowels: a, e, ı, i, o, ö, u and ü. Back vowels are a, ı, o, u; front vowels are e, i, ö, ü. The dotted and dotless letters are different: uppercase I matches lowercase ı, but uppercase İ matches lowercase i. Notice and write these letters accurately. We are not choosing suffixes yet.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: There are eight distinct written vowels. Back: a, ı, o, u. Front: e, i, ö, ü. The group labels describe vowels; no suffix rule is introduced here.
rule_blocks.pattern: Back: a ı o u | Front: e i ö ü
usage_notes_en: Look at the written vowel, not its nearest English look-alike.
A word can contain more than one vowel. Identifying them does not yet mean choosing a suffix.
common_errors_en: Calling ı the letter i loses the dotless/dotted contrast.
Putting ö or ü in the back group confuses the two groups.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Turkish capital I has no dot and becomes ı in lowercase. Capital İ has a dot and becomes i in lowercase. Other vowel pairs are A/a, E/e, O/o, Ö/ö, U/u and Ü/ü.
rule_blocks.pattern: A↔a | E↔e | I↔ı | İ↔i | O↔o | Ö↔ö | U↔u | Ü↔ü
usage_notes_en: Preserve the dot even when you capitalise a word.
Turkish-specific casing is required; English-only casing is unreliable for I/İ.
common_errors_en: İşık is not the correct capitalised spelling of ışık; write Işık.
Inek is not the correct capitalised spelling of inek; write İnek.

contexts.setting_en: At school, Ayşe and Mehmet compare initial capitals on word cards.

lines.speaker: Ayşe
lines.translation_en: “Işık” starts with capital I; “İnek” starts with capital İ.

lines.speaker: Mehmet
lines.translation_en: Capital I pairs with dotless ı; capital İ pairs with dotted i.

contexts.setting_en: Ayşe makes a short spelling note beside her shopping list.

lines.speaker: Ayşe
lines.target: Süt: ü. Su: u. Üzüm: ü.
lines.translation_en: “Süt” has ü; “su” has u; “üzüm” has ü.

examples.note_en: The three a letters are back vowels.
Both e letters are front vowels.
Capital I and lowercase ı belong together.
Capital İ and lowercase i belong together.
The vowels o and u are both back vowels.
Ü/ü is a front vowel; it is not u.
The vowels a and ı are both back vowels.
The vowels e and i are both front vowels.

exercises.prompt_en: Which lowercase letter pairs with capital I?

options.explanation_en: Correct letter or category.
Dotted i belongs to uppercase İ, not I.
u is a different back vowel.
ü is a front vowel.

hint_steps: Think about the presence or absence of a dot.
Capital I has no dot.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Capital I has no dot. Its lowercase partner is ı, not i.
exercises.explanation_en: I ↔ ı in Turkish.

exercises.prompt_en: Which uppercase letter pairs with lowercase i?

options.explanation_en: I is the capital of ı.
Correct letter or category.
U is the capital of u.
Ö is the capital of ö.

hint_steps: Keep the dot in the uppercase partner.
Look for the dotted capital letter.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Lowercase i has a dot. Its uppercase partner is İ, not I.
exercises.explanation_en: İ ↔ i in Turkish.

exercises.prompt_en: Which option is a back vowel?

options.explanation_en: e is a front vowel.
ö is a front vowel.
Correct letter or category.
ü is a front vowel.

hint_steps: Recall the two groups of four.
Back vowels include a and ı.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Only a is a back vowel here; e, ö and ü are all front vowels.
exercises.explanation_en: a, ı, o and u are back vowels.

exercises.prompt_en: Which option is a front vowel?

options.explanation_en: o is a back vowel.
u is a back vowel.
a is a back vowel.
Correct letter or category.

hint_steps: Think of the group containing e and i.
The front group also includes ö and ü.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Only ü is a front vowel here; o, u and a are all back vowels.
exercises.explanation_en: e, i, ö and ü are front vowels.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel occurs three times in araba? Type the vowel.
hint_steps: Look at every vowel in the word.
The repeated vowel is the first letter.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Read araba letter by letter: a-r-a-b-a. The repeated vowel is a.
exercises.explanation_en: araba contains a three times.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel appears twice in ekmek?
hint_steps: Find the two syllables.
The first and fourth letters match.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: In ekmek, the first and fourth letters are e. Keep the same vowel.
exercises.explanation_en: ekmek has two e vowels.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel is repeated in ışık?
hint_steps: Look for dots, not sounds.
Both vowels are dotless.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The two vowels in ışık are dotless ı. Dotted i would change the word.
exercises.explanation_en: ışık uses ı twice; it is not i.

exercises.prompt_en: What is the first vowel in inek?
hint_steps: Check the very first letter.
The opening vowel has a dot.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: inek begins with dotted i, not dotless ı.
exercises.explanation_en: inek starts with dotted i.

exercises.prompt_en: What is the first vowel in okul?
hint_steps: Read the first syllable.
The first vowel is rounded and is not u.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: okul begins with o; its second vowel is u.
exercises.explanation_en: okul starts with o and also contains u.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel appears in göz?

options.explanation_en: Correct letter or category.
o lacks the two dots of ö.
u is a different back vowel.
ü is another front vowel.

hint_steps: Check the printed dots above the vowel.
The vowel is dotted and rounded.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: göz uses ö with two dots, not undotted o or another rounded vowel.
exercises.explanation_en: göz contains ö, a front vowel.

exercises.prompt_en: In the shopping note, which vowel does su contain?
hint_steps: Look only at the middle item.
The word has one back vowel.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: su contains u. The two dots belong to ü, as in süt.
exercises.explanation_en: The only vowel in su is u.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel appears in süt?

options.explanation_en: u is the undotted vowel in su, not süt.
Correct letter or category.
ö is front but not the vowel in süt.
ı is dotless, but not present in süt.

hint_steps: Compare the shopping words su and süt.
The milk word has two dots above its vowel.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: süt contains ü. Do not confuse it with the u of su.
exercises.explanation_en: süt has the front vowel ü.

exercises.prompt_en: Type the final vowel in kapı.
hint_steps: Look at the ending.
The final vowel has no dot.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The final vowel of kapı is dotless ı, not dotted i.
exercises.explanation_en: kapı ends in dotless ı.

exercises.prompt_en: Type the first vowel in şehir.
hint_steps: Read the word from the start.
The first vowel appears after ş.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: şehir contains e first and i second. Read from the beginning.
exercises.explanation_en: şehir contains e followed by i; both are front vowels.

exercises.prompt_en: Complete the Turkish word for “milk” by supplying only its missing vowel.
hint_steps: The letter differs from the vowel in su.
Add the two dots above u.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The Turkish spelling of milk is süt, with ü rather than u or ö.
exercises.explanation_en: The correct word is süt, with ü.

exercises.prompt_en: Complete the Turkish word for “light” by supplying only its missing vowel.
hint_steps: The missing vowel matches the first vowel.
Use the dotless i-shaped letter.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The word is ışık: both vowels are dotless ı, not dotted i.
exercises.explanation_en: The correct word is ışık, with two dotless ı letters.

exercises.prompt_en: On a spelling card for “work”, which uppercase letter corresponds to its first vowel?

options.explanation_en: A is the capital of a, not i.
E is the capital of e, not i.
Correct letter or category.
I pairs with dotless ı, not dotted i.

hint_steps: The first letter is dotted.
Preserve the dot in the capital letter.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The first vowel in iş is dotted i; uppercase it as İ, not I.
exercises.explanation_en: iş starts with i, whose capital form is İ.

exercises.prompt_en: On a spelling card for “wet”, which uppercase letter corresponds to its first vowel?

options.explanation_en: U is the capital of u.
A is the capital of a.
İ pairs with dotted i, not dotless ı.
Correct letter or category.

hint_steps: The first vowel has no dot.
Its uppercase form also has no dot.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The first vowel in ıslak is dotless ı; uppercase it as I, not İ.
exercises.explanation_en: ıslak starts with ı, whose capital form is I.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel appears in kız? Type it.
hint_steps: It is a back vowel.
It resembles i but has no dot.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The single vowel in kız is dotless ı. Do not type i.
exercises.explanation_en: kız contains dotless ı.

exercises.prompt_en: Which vowel appears in göl? Type it.
hint_steps: It is a front vowel.
It is o with two dots above.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: The single vowel in göl is ö. It needs both dots.
exercises.explanation_en: göl contains front vowel ö.

exercises.instruction_en: Write the two groups from memory; check your work yourself.
exercises.prompt_target: a, e, ı, i, o, ö, u, ü
exercises.prompt_en: Without looking at the table, sort all eight Turkish vowels into back and front groups. Check your own grouping afterwards.
hint_steps: There are four vowels in each group.
The back set includes a and ı; the front set includes e and i.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Compare your work with the criteria.
exercises.explanation_en: Back: a, ı, o, u. Front: e, i, ö, ü.

criteria_en: All eight vowels are present exactly once.
Back contains a, ı, o, u.
Front contains e, i, ö, ü.
The dots on i/ı and o/ö and u/ü are exact.

exercises.instruction_en: Write two familiar Turkish words without help; self-check.
exercises.prompt_en: From memory, write two different familiar A1 words: one containing dotless ı and one containing dotted i. Then capitalise their first letter if it is a vowel. Self-check both words.
hint_steps: Choose one word for each vowel.
Remember that a starting ı takes I, while a starting i takes İ.
exercises.feedback_wrong_en: Compare your work with the criteria.
exercises.explanation_en: Possible models include ışık / Işık and inek / İnek. Other correctly spelt reviewed A1 words also count.

criteria_en: One genuine A1 word contains dotless ı.
A different genuine A1 word contains dotted i.
Both words are spelt with the correct Turkish dots.
If a word begins with ı or i, its initial capital is I or İ respectively.

vocabulary_audit.note: Standalone vowel glyphs are alphabet symbols rather than vocabulary lemmas. Turkish verb suffixes and question particles are not tested.

level_audit.note: Only alphabetic recognition, front/back grouping, and Turkish-specific upper/lowercase matching are taught. No suffix forms or detailed phonetics.

authoritative_sources_consulted.title: Ünlülerin Nitelikleri
authoritative_sources_consulted.verified_rule: The eight Turkish vowels are a, e, ı, i, o, ö, u, ü.

authoritative_sources_consulted.title: Ses, Harf ve Alfabe
authoritative_sources_consulted.verified_rule: Alphabet uses different letter pairs I/ı and İ/i.

authoritative_sources_consulted.title: Türkçenin Yabancı Dil Olarak Öğretimi Programı
authoritative_sources_consulted.verified_rule: A1 sound/orthography practice explicitly calls out ı–i distinction.

notes: Turkish locale-insensitive marking recognises vowel identity but does not enforce uppercase-only submissions; letter case pairs are therefore assessed with multiple choice rather than exact-match case conversion.
Two production questions are deliberately self-checked and unscored.
